name: Leela Palaces Hotels & Resorts Ltd
title: Leela Palaces Hotels & Resorts Ltd - 544408 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Leela posted 30% RevPAR and 36% EBITDA growth in Q2 on pricing power, but supply is pipeline-led (1,000+ keys, Srinagar/Bandhavgarh slipping to end-CY27), with H2 EBITDA guidance held at high-teens.

triggers.label: ADR growth 30%, RevPAR index 1.46x
triggers.quote: our RevPAR index expanded to 1.46x from 1.41x

triggers.label: H2 EBITDA high-teens, FY27 raised implicitly
triggers.quote: we definitely stay true on the guidance

triggers.label: Srinagar/Bandhavgarh opening slips to end-CY27
triggers.quote: Srinagar and Bandhavgarh would open towards the end of calendar year '27

triggers.label: Q3 RevPAR double-digit guided
triggers.quote: we are very much on track for double -digit growth in terms of RevPAR in Q3 as well

summary.headline: Leela Palaces Q2 FY27 operating EBITDA rose 36% to INR 1,877 million on 33% revenue growth; FY27 guidance kept at mid-to-high teens for H2.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 operating revenue rose 33% YoY to INR 4,119 million, with every revenue stream growing above 20%. Operating EBITDA grew 36% to INR 1,877 million at a 46% margin (up 118 bps), and PAT rose 27% to INR 946 million. RevPAR grew 30% and the company said it outperformed the India luxury market (17% vs 13% for April to August). Management reiterated mid-to-high teens EBITDA growth for H2 despite H1 running well ahead of guidance, and said the Mumbai BKC project needs incremental equity to buy the full FSI.

financial_highlights.change: from 1.6x in Mar 2026 and 3.7x in Mar 2025

segments.name: City hotels (H1)
segments.commentary: RevPAR grew 26% in H1 FY27; record H1 city occupancy of 74% vs 69% last year. Bengaluru, Chennai, Jaipur and Udaipur each grew at high double digits.

segments.name: Resorts (H1)
segments.commentary: RevPAR grew 18% in H1 FY27; same-store resort occupancy near 60%, with mid-50s blended including Coorg. Jaipur H1 occupancy above 60%.

segments.name: Owned domestic hotels (Q2)
segments.commentary: RevPAR up 30% with ADR up 30% to INR 25,046 and India headline occupancy of 69%. Domestic revenue at owned hotels grew more than 30%, and growth excluding Coorg was similar.

segments.name: Management fees
segments.commentary: Fees up 76% to INR 289 million; share of revenue rising from about 5% to 7%. Management said 85-90% of new managed-fee revenue flows to EBITDA.

segments.name: Dubai Palm Jumeirah JV (25% stake)
segments.commentary: Share of loss narrowed QoQ. The asset is EBITDA breakeven to positive; interest and depreciation keep it loss-making at PAT. Third-party operator runs it; renovation planned from around April 2027 for about 12 months.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 EBITDA growth guided at mid-to-high teens; management said H1 far exceeded the original mid-teens FY27 EBITDA guidance and the FY27 outcome should be much better than initially guided.
Management said Q3 is tracking ahead of pace with double-digit RevPAR growth expected; festive and long weekends in Oct-Nov support demand.
Corporate rate ask for CY27 is mid-to-high double digit; 60-70% of corporate static rates have moved to dynamic pricing.
Effective tax rate expected in the 20s% for FY27 after H1 at 16% of PBT (pre-JV share) due to Coorg deferred tax asset.
Target of over 5,200 keys by FY30 (about 2,600 owned, roughly 50:50 owned vs managed); FY30 EBITDA aspiration of INR 2,000 crore-odd cited on the call.
BKC Mumbai hotel commissioning reiterated for CY30; lease executed September 2026; Leela plans to seek shareholder approval for FSI purchase.
capex_capacity: Five contracted owned pipeline projects (Agra, Srinagar, Ayodhya, Ranthambore, Bandhavgarh) capex about INR 1,432 crore; INR 150 crore spent to date, about INR 450 crore by end FY27 and about INR 600 crore next year.

Openings: Jaisalmer and Leela Luxury Residences Mumbai in FY27 (residences first set of residents targeted in the last quarter of FY27); Arq Chennai to open this quarter; Srinagar and Bandhavgarh toward end of CY27; Agra, Ayodhya, Ranthambore and Sikkim in CY28; Tadoba around CY30.
More than 1,000 keys under development; 10 new openings across eight locations are contracted.

BKC Mumbai: 250-key Leela Palace plus 700k sq ft office, 50:50 JV with Brookfield; INR 800 crore committed capex (INR 400 crore equity, INR 400 crore debt) unchanged, though the FSI purchase could raise Leela's share above that.
Coorg (71 keys) rebranded as The Leela on 8 July 2026; EBITDA breakeven reached. Wellness itineraries launched recently.
demand_pricing: Suite occupancy up over 700 bps to mid-40s on paid basis; blended occupancy late 60s.
BRICS Summit boosted The Leela Palace New Delhi; management said the event was confined to Delhi and the ADR growth excluding it would still be high-teens.
Net Promoter Score 87 for H1 (about 13 points above the Asia-Pacific luxury average). RevPAR index rose to 1.46x from 1.41x; RevPAR premium about INR 4,500 over the luxury market.
Direct booking channel (brand website) rose to 15.1% of room revenue in H1 from 10.5% a year earlier.
International business low double-digit growth in Q2 excluding BRICS; management aims to return to a 50:50 India-to-international mix over time.
Dubai residences: 260-270 high-value transactions on Palm Jumeirah in recent months; sales timeline of 2-3 years unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Is the RevPAR outperformance sustainable, and when would occupancy be prioritised over ADR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited iconic, supply-constrained assets, NPS of 87, and broad-based growth with all segments up high double digits in rate and RevPAR. It said it has become more mindful on pricing but sees a long runway on ADR.

qa_highlights.question: Were FY27 EBITDA guidance and H2 growth rates being revised, given H1 EBITDA growth of about 38%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept mid-to-high teens EBITDA growth for H2 and said the full year would be well above the original mid-teens guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ESOP impact on costs and the flow-through?
qa_highlights.answer: ESOP expense started being booked from Q2, alongside headcount for new value drivers (Arq clubs, Azulian House) and the Coorg ramp-up. Excluding these, flow-through is about 60%. ESOP impact is slightly below INR 8 crore, though no exact figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the BKC capex rise from the INR 800 crore committed figure?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR 800 crore committed capex is unchanged. Leela's share will rise to fund the FSI purchase, and this will be trued up when shareholder approval for the demerger/divestment is obtained.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the ADR growth came from BRICS and other events?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said BRICS impacted only the Delhi asset and that ADR growth excluding it would have been high-teens. It expects a major compression event each year (G20, India Energy Week, AI Impact Summit, BRICS).

qa_highlights.question: What are Coorg's revenue and EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Coorg's ADR has roughly doubled versus the pre-branding period. The asset has reached EBITDA breakeven but no revenue or EBITDA figure was disclosed.

risks_watch: Dubai JV: ADRs still lagging on weak international demand; the asset goes into renovation around April 2027 for about 12 months, with EBITDA visibility only after rebranding.
BKC: material related-party transaction needing shareholder approval; office-stake divestment terms undetermined; funding may rise above the INR 800 crore committed capex.
Coorg still ramping; EBITDA at breakeven only.
Mid-to-high teens H2 guidance implies a sharp slowdown from the 36% Q2 EBITDA growth, against a high H2 base.
Dependence on compression events for ADR; the company says the BRICS effect was confined to Delhi.
Corporate rate renewals for CY27 are still under negotiation.
Effective tax rate guided to the 20s% in FY27, up from 16% in H1.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on demand, pricing power and the pipeline. Management was more guarded on Dubai ADRs, the BKC capex and the Dubai EBITDA, which it declined to quantify citing a third-party operator.
key_quotes: Q2 FY27 was another quarter of exceptional performance for The Leela.
We delivered 30% RevPAR growth, 33% growth in operating revenue, and 36% growth in operating EBITDA; a second consecutive quarter of 35% plus EBITDA growth.
Excluding ESOP and excluding Coorg because Coorg is also stabilizing and it's not giving the EBITDA numbers as Jaipur and Udaipur, flow-through would be around 60% for the quarter.
We are very much on track for double-digit growth in terms of RevPAR in Q3 as well.

adds.what: Leela Luxury Residences Mumbai, first residents targeted Q4 FY27
Srinagar and Bandhavgarh hotels, toward end of CY27
Agra, Ayodhya, Ranthambore and Sikkim hotels in CY28 (five contracted owned pipeline projects capex about INR 1,432 crore in total)

growth.why: Management reiterated mid-to-high teens H2 FY27 EBITDA growth after H1 EBITDA rose 38%, with Q3 RevPAR guided at double-digit growth backed by demand, dynamic pricing and contracted pipeline (INR 1,432 crore capex, 10 openings contracted), though the brief gives no explicit FY27 revenue number and most new keys arrive in CY27-CY28.
